key_insight: RECAST reconstructs a black-box model from limited data by using counterfactual examples as geometry-aware support points in a Wasserstein-based surrogate, improving fidelity when standard reconstruction methods struggle.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical auditing tool for fairness and accountability when direct access to the target system is restricted and query budgets are limited.
method: Builds a behavioral surrogate using Wasserstein barycentric prototypes.
Incorporates counterfactuals for both classes to reduce decision-boundary shift in low-sample regimes.
Supports group fairness diagnostics without requiring online access during reconstruction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on real-world datasets and multiple setups showing high fidelity, strong query efficiency, and stable performance under limited and noisy access.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on the quality and representativeness of available counterfactuals, especially when data are very sparse or noisy.
paper_title: RECAST: Model Reconstruction via Counterfactual-Aware Wasserstein Geometry under Limited Data
